zotero.abstractNote: Introduction: Psychotherapy is an effective treatment for mental disorders, but a significant proportion of patients do not respond to treatment. Identifying these non-respondent patients early is a major challenge in clinical practice. The research unit 5187 PREACT (Precision Psychotherapy for Non-Respondent Patients: From Signatures to Predictions to Clinical Utility) aims to develop and validate predictive models for treatment response in psychotherapy. Methods: This study protocol describes the design and methods of the research unit, which integrates clinical, neuroimaging, and digital phenotyping data to identify signatures of non-response. The research unit comprises several subprojects focusing on different aspects of psychotherapy, including cognitive-behavioral therapy and psychodynamic therapy. The study will involve a large-scale longitudinal assessment of patients with various mental disorders. Discussion: The findings of the PREACT research unit are expected to provide a basis for precision psychotherapy, enabling clinicians to tailor treatment to individual patient needs and improve outcomes for non-respondent patients.
